chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, raising it (mursal), from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), said:

When God bestows a bounty upon His servant and it appears upon him (with gratitude), he is named a beloved of God who speaks of God's bounty; and when God bestows a bounty upon a servant and it does not appear upon him, he is named the one hated by God, a denier of God's bounty.

key_terms.بَغِيض اللَّه: hated by God — one who is in a state of divine displeasure
key_terms.حَبِيب اللَّه: beloved of God — one who stands in a state of divine favour and love
key_terms.مُحَدِّث بِنِعْمَة: one who speaks of the bounty — one who acknowledges and narrates God's favours
key_terms.مُكَذِّب: denier/one who belies — one who implicitly denies a blessing by not acknowledging it
key_terms.نِعْمَة: bounty/blessing — God's material and spiritual gifts to a person

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about displaying God's blessings and gratitude in Shi'a hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that openly displaying the blessings God has bestowed — through gratitude and acknowledgment — earns one the status of a beloved of God. Conversely, concealing or failing to acknowledge God's blessings is equivalent to denying them, making one an object of divine displeasure. This hadith was delivered to the early Shi'a community, who understood 'displaying the bounty' not as arrogant show, but as sincere gratitude and thankfulness (shukr) visible in one's manner, speech, and conduct.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad raising it, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:

‘When Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Favours upon His<sup>azwj</sup> servant with a Bounty, and he displays it (with thanks), he is named as a Beloved of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> narrating with a Bounty of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>; and when Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Favours upon a servant with a Bounty, so he does not display it (with thanks), he is named as the one being angry with Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, a denier in a Bounty of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from in a marfu‘ manner the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has stated this Hadith.

‘If Allah grants a bounty to one of His servants and such bounty appears on him, he is called the friend of Allah who speaks of the bounty of Allah. If Allah grants a bounty to one of His servants but it does not appear on him, he is called the anger of Allah and denying the bounty of Allah.’”
